title: Canonical monomorphism between consecutive nilpotent-units kernels
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], N its nilradical, and E_j the kernels of [def-sc-reduction-units-power-kernel]. The inclusion N^(j+2) ⊆ N^(j+1) induces V(N^(j+1)) → V(N^(j+2)). Restriction of units along its base changes annihilates E_(j+1) on V(N^(j+1)). Define e_j:E_(j+1)→E_j by the kernel universal property so that its composite with E_j→Gm is E_(j+1)→Gm. This constructed morphism is monic.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 and the following Claim; proof text retained in the parent DAG node

proof.text: On each affine open N^(j+2)=N^(j+1)N is contained in N^(j+1), by Ideal.mul_le_left. IdealSheafData.inclusion gives the corresponding inclusion of closed subschemes.

Over an etale object U→X form the map between the two pullbacks using identity on U and the subscheme inclusion. Its composite with the first projection is the first projection, by pullback.lift_fst. Apply the contravariant global sections functor and the units additive-group functor to this equality. Composing the next kernel inclusion gives zero by kernel.condition, hence restriction to the preceding subscheme also gives zero. Equality of sheaf morphisms is checked componentwise.
Use kernel.lift to define e_j from this zero equation. The equation e_j≫(E_j→Gm)=(E_(j+1)→Gm) is kernel.lift_ι. Since the right-hand side is monic, mono_of_mono_fac proves e_j monic.
